articles.text:
AFTER LOSING his mother inthe stampede at the Maha Kumbh on January 29, Dhananjay Kumar Gond (24) returned home to Bihar's Gopalganj - only to be told by the local administration and the police that he needed her death certificate towrapup the formalities. He retumed to Prayagrajon Monday and has since been making desperate rounds of hospitals and govemment offices - but in vain. With little clarity on who will issue death certificates, Dhananjayis one of several family members of stampede victims who have beenrunning pillar to post in Prayagraj. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has announced a compensationof Rs 25 lakh foreach victim's family. articles.headline_raw:
To check doping and age
fraud, Govt scraps cash
awards for junior athletes
articles.body_raw:
MIHIRVASAVDA
MUMBAI FEBRUARY 7

JUNIOR ATHLETES winning in-
ternational medals will no
longer receive cash awards from
the government. This major
Sports Ministry policy shift,
which came into effect on
February 1, is aimed at tackling
the twin menace of doping and
age fraud as well as “keeping the
hunger of youngsters alive".

According to theold system, a
gold medal at the World
Championship would fetch ajun-
ior athlete approximately Rs 13
lakh while a top of the podium
finish at Asian or Commonweakh
had acash prize of Rs 5 lakh.
A Sports Ministry official said
oneof the key factors behind this
decision was to promote junior
competitions as developmental
events rather than making it all
about a podium finish.
CONTINUED ONPAGE 2
articles.headline: To check doping and age fraud, Govt scraps cash awards for junior athletes
articles.text:
JUNIOR ATHLETES winning international medals will no longer receive cash awards from the government. This major Sports Ministry policy shift, which came into effect on February 1, is aimed at tackling the twin menace of doping and age fraud as well as "keeping the hunger of youngsters alive".

According to theold system, a gold medal at the World Championship would fetch ajunior athlete approximately Rs 13 lakh while a top of the podium finish at Asian or Commonweakh had acash prize of Rs 5 lakh. A Sports Ministry official said oneof the key factors behind this decision was to promote junior competitions as developmental events rather than making it all about a podium finish.
